_note: Read by ios/scripts/appstore-metadata.mjs. Mike reads this before anything is submitted. Keep name and subtitle <= 30, keywords <= 100 and promotional text <= 170 characters, with no em dashes. The app is found by bundle id (ios/scripts/appstore-lib.mjs). The review contact's phone comes from ~/.config/poddle/review-contact.json, not from here. Copy is written as Mike (~/.claude/skills/mike-voice). No Claude or Codex in the name, subtitle or keywords: other companies' trademarks there are a common rejection (guideline 2.3.7); the description and notes can say what it works with. Notifications aren't promised in the description: in 1.0 only a deployment holding Mike's push key can send them (docs/setup-and-updates.md 2.4).
name: Threadbear
subtitle: Your agent threads on iPhone
_category: Developer Tools first: it's the phone side of a Mac app for running AI coding agents. Productivity second, for the inbox and replying on the go.
_contentRights: The app shows only what the person's own agents wrote, from their own deployment, and the made-up sample threads, so no third-party content.
promotionalText: The iPhone app for Threadbear, a Mac app I made for running AI coding agents. Reply, approve a command or answer a question when you're away from your desk.
_whatsNew: What's New for the version being prepared, as Mike. Rewrite it for every version. Left out on the first version, which App Store Connect doesn't allow it on.
whatsNew:
A few bits since the last one:

- Replies can now show diagrams and little web pages, and Slack or email drafts show line for line with a Copy button
- You can pick which Mac a new thread runs on, and put your Macs in the order you like
- Messages waiting for a Mac that's offline show up in the thread, and you can cancel them
- The mic shows a waveform and how long you've been talking, with a small stop button
- You can add your own words for dictation to get right, in Settings
- Copy a thread's ID, and paste one into a message to link to that thread
- Ask no longer talks about my own setup (Agent Archive and Tailscale), it just says your Ask server and links to how to run one

Hopefully you like it, and if anything's broken let me know at threadbear@mikecann.app
description:
This is the iPhone app for Threadbear, a Mac app I made for running Claude Code and Codex threads on my own subscriptions. The Mac does all the work, and this lets me keep an eye on it from the couch or when I'm out.

You get your inbox, with the threads that need you at the top, and the latest messages in each one. You can reply, approve or deny a command an agent wants to run, answer the questions it asks, and start a new thread in one of your folders. Threads you're done with for now can hibernate until later or go in the Den, the same as on the Mac. If your Mac's asleep, anything you send waits until it's back.

You need Threadbear running on a Mac to pair it with. The phone talks to the Convex deployment your Mac uses, with a sign in code you make on the Mac, and none of it comes to me. If you just want a look first, tap "Look around with sample threads" on the first screen.

It's my own tool and still pretty new, so if something's broken or confusing, email me at threadbear@mikecann.app. Hopefully you like it!

ageRating._note: Nothing objectionable: the person's own agent threads and made-up sample ones. Nobody else's content is shown and there's no way to talk to other people, so userGeneratedContent and messagingAndChat are false. No browser in the app, so unrestrictedWebAccess is false. Questions the API doesn't have yet are answered in App Store Connect: all none. Unknown keys are skipped, and keys Apple adds later are left as they are.

review.notes:
Thanks for taking a look at Threadbear.

TRYING IT
Tap "Look around with sample threads" at the bottom of the first screen. It opens the app on made-up threads that only live on the phone, so you can try everything without pairing. You can open a thread and reply, tap Allow or Deny on the command in "Release 1.2 of the garden app", answer the question in "Where should the settings live?", start a new thread with the button at the top right, and swipe a thread to hibernate it or put it in the Den. A sample thread answers a couple of seconds after you send it something. The menu at the top left has Settings, and "Leave the demo" goes back to the first screen.

WHAT IT IS
The app is the companion to Threadbear on the Mac, which runs AI coding agents (Claude Code and Codex) on the person's own Mac and their own subscriptions. The Mac app keeps each thread's status and latest messages in the person's own Convex deployment, and this app reads and replies through it. Pairing needs that Mac app: it shows a QR code with the deployment's address and a sign in code made for the phone. There's no account or sign-in with me, so there's no demo account. I can't give you a pairing code either, as it would open someone's real deployment with their real work in it, which is why the sample threads are there.

PERMISSIONS
- Camera: to scan the pairing code on the Mac, and to take a photo after tapping + and Take Photo in a reply.
- Microphone and speech recognition: only after tapping Dictate on a new thread or the mic beside Send in a reply, or for Ask, after pressing its button or tapping the mic in an Ask thread.
- Notifications: only asked once it's paired with a Mac, for when a thread needs you. Never asked in the sample threads.
- Location, while using the app: only asked once a card in the Pocket (the wallet button at the top of the inbox) names a place, to mark that card "here" and bring it to the front when you're near. It's used on the phone and in Apple's map search, and never sent to the app's backend. Never asked in the sample threads.

OTHER
No ads, no tracking, no analytics and no in-app purchases. The app only talks to the deployment it's paired with.
